title: Getting to know each other
subTitle: Answer the questions in BreakOut Rooms (BORs):
bulletPoints: Pick a timekeeper. A minute per each tops
Tell each other a bit about yourself (name, job, location etc.). Feel free to ask additional questions.
Share your own experience of learning English from movies.

title: Tips to enhance your experience
tiles: Below, you'll find several sections with questions. You can discuss them in any order (or even skip some!)
Always finish your answer with a question to your speaking partners (ex. "And what about you?")
Keep an eye on the timer so you have enough time to discuss the most interesting questions.
Assign one member to share the screen (This page).

title: All aboard! We're getting started.
subTitle: We have 45 minutes for this section.
numberPoints: Discussion. We'll discuss the pros and cons of this learning method.
Screen test. A scene from an HBO TV show.
Breaking down some key words and expressions from the scene.

title: Do you watch movies without translation?
bulletPoints: + if you've watched a movie or show in English in the last month

title: Why watch films in the original?
subTitle: Three big reasons.
numberPoints: It's a gentle introduction to the language.
You can hear the continuous speech (the light version of language immersion).

You get to enjoy the original acting, story and jokes. (wordplay and double meanings)
instead of translation.

title: Challenging part
numberPoints: The movies are not usually designed for teaching.
The plot and the speech are a constant flow.
Acting is not always natural. There's sometimes exaggerated performance and non-everyday conversations.

title: Do you watch movies with subtitles?
bulletPoints: R if you usually use Russian subtitles

title: How to solve the issues?
numberPoints: Rewatch. Multiple times. Fill in the gaps with each viewing.
Eventually, start listening to those movies in the background instead of music.
Repeat new terms or phrases you've just learned out loud.
Choose content that's personally relevant to you.
Go back to movies you already know with translation — you'll make a lot of discoveries along with learning the language.

title: Let's shift to practice
text:
We'll see a scene from HBO's TV series "Silicon Valley" about IT and startups created by Mike Judge, known for Idiocracy and Office Space.
He combined his own experience as an engineer in the Valley with the work of 200 consultants to create a realistic satire of the VC and software world.
